questions.prompt: A browser follows an application's redirect to Okta. Who sends the resulting request to Okta?

options.text: The browser following the supplied redirect
options.explanation: The app gives direction; the browser performs this next HTTP delivery.

options.text: The app directly sends that redirected browser request
options.explanation: A redirect is not itself a server-to-server delivery.

options.text: The identity record sends the request
options.explanation: An identity record is data, not an HTTP participant.

options.text: Okta creates the incoming browser request
options.explanation: The browser initiates the redirected request to the provider.

review.heading: Your browser asks; a server responds

questions.prompt: An HTTP trace shows a 403 returned by the business application. Why identify the responding system?

options.text: The status describes that receiver's operation, not every upstream stage
options.explanation: A target denial does not by itself locate an Okta authentication failure.

options.text: Every 403 always comes from Okta
options.explanation: Different participants can return HTTP responses.

options.text: A 403 identifies the missing business permission by itself
options.explanation: The status alone does not identify the exact rule or cause.

options.text: The responder is irrelevant once a status exists
options.explanation: Source and operation context are essential to interpretation.

review.heading: Read the destination before interpreting the result

questions.prompt: A browser receives HTTP 302 with a Location header during sign-in. What does this normally direct it to do?

options.text: Make a new request to the indicated location
options.explanation: A redirect directs navigation; it is not itself proof that the final application accepted sign-in.

options.text: Create a local application session immediately
options.explanation: Session creation needs the actual app's acceptance process.

options.text: Treat Location as the user's employee identifier
options.explanation: The header is a navigation destination, not a subject identifier.

options.text: Assume every later step succeeded
options.explanation: A redirect is only one step in a longer exchange.

review.heading: A response can send the browser elsewhere

questions.prompt: An HTTP POST reaches an application's endpoint and returns 200. What needs context before calling sign-in successful?

options.text: What operation the receiver processed and what application outcome it recorded
options.explanation: An HTTP success status does not universally mean identity acceptance or resource permission.

options.text: Only whether the page title looks familiar
options.explanation: Presentation is not a processing result.

options.text: Only whether a previous user succeeded last week
options.explanation: A different attempt cannot establish this one's outcome.

options.text: Nothing; every 200 means full application access
options.explanation: Status meaning depends on the operation and returned result.

review.heading: A status code describes a request's result

questions.prompt: Two users sign in within the same second. How should an analyst associate a log event with the intended attempt?

options.text: Use relevant user, app, time and transaction identifiers together
options.explanation: Nearby timestamps alone are weak association when activity overlaps.

options.text: Choose the closest timestamp regardless of user
options.explanation: That can attach another person's result to the case.

options.text: Assume the latest event belongs to the open ticket
options.explanation: Recency does not establish the intended transaction.

options.text: Use only the application's display name
options.explanation: A shared name does not identify one attempt or instance.

review.heading: Match the evidence to the right attempt

evidence: User A and user B both act at 10:00:00 UTC
Relevant ticket: user A, app instance X, request R71
Nearby event: user B, app instance Y, request R72

questions.prompt: An Okta event reports successful SSO issuance. Which result still needs receiver evidence?

options.text: Application acceptance and the intended local account/session outcome
options.explanation: Issuing identity information differs from consuming it successfully.

options.text: Whether the issuer recorded issuance
options.explanation: That is the observed event outcome.

options.text: Whether the browser can ever carry messages
options.explanation: That general capability does not answer this downstream question.

options.text: Whether all source profiles are synchronized
options.explanation: Issuance does not establish unrelated source-data operations.

review.heading: Read an event as a sentence first

questions.prompt: A System Log query returns no matching events. What is an appropriate next check?

options.text: Org, time range, time zone, filters and actual entry path
options.explanation: An empty search may reflect search scope rather than absence of processing.

options.text: Conclude no identity activity occurred anywhere
options.explanation: The query cannot support that universal claim.

options.text: Remove all app assignments immediately
options.explanation: That change is unrelated to understanding the search result.

options.text: Assume the target application must be working
options.explanation: An empty issuer query proves no target outcome.

review.heading: Choose a search that answers the question

questions.prompt: The browser reaches an app, which logs a failed audience check after Okta issuance succeeded. Where is the first confirmed failure?

options.text: The receiving application's federation acceptance
options.explanation: The supplied progression succeeds through issuance and fails at receiver targeting validation.

options.text: The original credential check necessarily failed
options.explanation: The evidence locates a later boundary.

options.text: The target account was necessarily deleted
options.explanation: No account-lifecycle evidence is supplied.

options.text: The browser never delivered the response
options.explanation: The receiver's rejection establishes it processed a return.

review.heading: Follow Maya's attempt one step at a time

evidence: Provider issuance: succeeded for request R81
Browser return: reaches the intended app ACS
Receiver result: audience mismatch; local session not created

questions.prompt: A saved connection setting matches a design document. What has not yet been proved?

options.text: That the live operation used it and produced the intended target outcome
options.explanation: Saved state and runtime behavior require different evidence.

options.text: That the saved value matches the document
options.explanation: That comparison is supplied directly.

options.text: That configuration can influence processing
options.explanation: It can influence behavior, but execution is the missing evidence.

options.text: That a target result should be checked
options.explanation: Checking the target is the appropriate next boundary.

review.heading: Read the destination before interpreting the result

questions.prompt: A sign-in failed shortly after a mapping change. What makes blaming the change premature?

options.text: Timing alone does not establish which operation or boundary failed
options.explanation: Correlated processing evidence is needed to link the change to the outcome.

options.text: Changes can never cause sign-in failures
options.explanation: They can; the point is to establish the connection.

options.text: A failed attempt always has several unrelated causes
options.explanation: The cause count is unknown until investigated.

options.text: A familiar error message identifies the exact cause
options.explanation: Similar messages can hide different failure boundaries.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.

review.heading: Match the evidence to the right attempt

questions.prompt: An engineer applies one justified correction. What makes the retest useful?

options.text: A fresh controlled attempt with relevant starting state and correlated target results
options.explanation: A retest must exercise the changed boundary and verify the intended outcome.

options.text: Refresh an unrelated public page
options.explanation: That does not exercise the identity operation.

options.text: Only confirm the setting saved
options.explanation: Saving does not prove runtime acceptance.

options.text: Reuse an old app session without checking new messages
options.explanation: Existing session access can bypass the changed federation path.

review.heading: Follow Maya's attempt one step at a time

questions.prompt: A record shows a provisioning request was submitted, but no response or target read is supplied. What can be concluded?

options.text: Submission is established; completion and target state remain unknown
options.explanation: A proposed or initiated action is not a verified outcome.

options.text: The target update definitely succeeded
options.explanation: No completion evidence is provided.

options.text: The target update definitely failed
options.explanation: Missing result does not prove failure either.

options.text: The user's next sign-in must use the new value
options.explanation: The packet establishes no such downstream effect.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.

review.heading: Compare a redirect with account management
